interview.hardest_part: Maintaining accurate road position and heading through successive corners using only one-second discrete inputs, especially after speed builds or the car begins sliding. The challenge compounds across five stages with no retry.
interview.likely_failure: An off-road excursion, collision, or spin leads to repeated poor corrections and lost wall-clock time; later stages are then left incomplete. A smaller risk is hesitating or choosing Enter incorrectly on transition screens.
interview.helpful_mechanics: The top-down view exposes the upcoming road, automatic transmission simplifies driving, braking/reverse permits recovery, and automatic recovery can rescue some excursions. There is no pace requirement for checkpoints, the game pauses while decisions are made, and Enter provides straightforward result navigation.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Full-second held inputs prevent fine analog throttle and steering modulation, while vehicle inertia and low-grip slides make corrections delayed and easy to overdo. Scenery can trap or deflect the car, manual recovery/restart and in-race pause are disabled, there is only one attempt, and thinking/rendering time consumes the same three-hour budget needed to finish all five stages.
